merger_description:
Experience Australia Group Pty Ltd (**EAG**) proposes to acquire, by way of share and asset purchases, a portfolio of tourism assets (**Tourism Portfolio**) from Kelsian Group Limited or its subsidiaries or controlled entities (together, **Kelsian**) (the **Acquisition**).

  

EAG operates a range of tourism businesses across Australia under the brand name “Journey Beyond”. EAG’s tourism businesses include tours, accommodation, rail journeys, scenic flights, and marine sightseeing.

  

EAG’s subsidiary, Outback Spirit Tours Pty Ltd (Outback Spirit), supplies touring packages to remote destinations across Western Australia, the Northern Territory, Queensland and South Australia.

  

Kelsian is an ASX-listed global operator of bus, motorcoach, tourism and marine services. In Australia, it supplies public transport services across six states and territories through Transit Systems, and marine transport services (including commuter and leisure ferries) through SeaLink Marine & Tourism.

  

In April 2025, Kelsian announced an intention to divest its Australian tourism assets, known as the Tourism Portfolio. In February 2026, Kelsian announced it had entered into binding agreements for the sale of the companies and businesses forming its Tourism Portfolio to EAG.

Kelsian’s Tourism Portfolio comprises:

* Adelaide Sightseeing Tours: tour services in the Adelaide region
* Murray Princess Cruise: cruise experiences along the Murray River
* Tasmania Ferries: ferry services between Bruny Island and Tasmania mainland
* Sydney Harbour Cruises and Ferries: harbour cruise and ferry services in Sydney
* K'gari Resorts, Tours and Ferries: resort accommodation, tour and ferry services on K'gari (Fraser Island)
* Northern Territory Ferries: ferry and boat services in the Northern Territory
* Swan River Cruises: cruise and charter services operating from the Barrack Street Jetty in Perth
* Swan Valley Tours: river cruise and coach tour services from Perth to the Swan Valley
* Bells Functions: waterfront function and event space at the Barrack Street Jetty in Perth

In addition, the Tourism Portfolio includes SeaLink Rottnest, the passenger ferry service from Perth and Fremantle to Rottnest Island.  


In relation to this Acquisition, Journey Beyond and Kelsian overlap in the supply of tourism experiences in Sydney, the Whitsundays, K'gari and South Australia.   


Outback Spirit currently purchases accommodation and ferry services from Kelsian in K'gari and Bruny Island.  


ACCC is also assessing EAG’s proposed acquisition of SeaLink Rottnest.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents provided by the parties, market
feedback and publicly available information.
The ACCC notes that EAG initially proposed to acquire SeaLink
Rottnest and separately notified that acquisition to the ACCC. On 26
August 2026, Kelsian publicly announced that it had agreed with
EAG not to proceed with the SeaLink Rottnest acquisition and that it
intended to continue operating the business. The ACCC’s
assessment of that acquisition ceased on 26 August 2026.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings:
• There is limited overlap between the tourism experiences the
Parties offer or the Parties’ tourism experiences are
substantially differentiated and do not appear to compete
particularly closely.
• The merged firm would likely continue to face competition from
alternative suppliers of tourism experiences in the areas of
overlap.
• The merged firm would be unlikely to have an ability and
incentive to foreclose rivals’ access to accommodation, tour or
ferry services given there are alternative suppliers.
With respect to the supply of ferry services to Rottnest Island, the
ACCC considered whether the separation of Kelsian’s SeaLink
Rottnest from the tourism businesses and assets the subject of the
Acquisition could weaken its competitive position and/or increase
the likelihood of its exit. This could occur due to the loss of
synergies between SeaLink Rottnest and the other businesses
included in the tourism portfolio being sold to EAG as part of the
Acquisition.
The ACCC noted the information provided by Kelsian that SeaLink
Rottnest is operationally independent from the tourism portfolio,
complementary to Kelsian’s retained SeaLink operations and
profitable. The ACCC also noted representations made by Kelsian
Group CEO, both publicly and separately to the ACCC, that Kelsian
intends to continue operating SeaLink Rottnest. On this basis, the
ACCC concluded that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of
substantially lessening competition in the supply of ferry services to
Rottnest Island.
